patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-001: handler accepts `now_slot` from instruction data. Authenticate against Clock::get()?.slot before use — caller-controlled clocks enable permanent DoS of permissionless cranks. Two confirmed-exploitable bounty wins in this class: percolator-prog#107 (ACTIVATE, fixed 6512fa1) + percolator-cli#78 F33 (RETIRE, fixed 3fd9b1d). See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-001.
exclusions: the caller-supplied slot/timestamp is authenticated against Clock::get()?.slot (e.g. clamped/rejected) before any use
the value is provably discarded — never written to an account, emitted in an event, or used in a later gate (a positive 'not persisted' proof, not merely 'this handler does not seem to use it')

the handler is gated to an admin that must SIGN AND is bound by an explicit constraint to a hardcoded / program-stored admin key (constraint = signer.key() == config.admin, or has_one = admin WHERE admin is declared Signer<>) — a bare Signer<> with no such binding is a user-supplied key the caller self-assigns and is NOT sufficient, nor is a key-equality/has_one check on a non-signer account — AND the value is never re-read by a permissionless crank or downstream instruction

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-002: cross-market aggregate counter. Verify EVERY write to this field is gated by per-market authorization — permissionless cross-market inflation enables insurance-fund drain. Documented public class (percolator-prog#104); not a Jelleo bounty win — included because the pattern is reproducible across perp-DEX programs. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-002.
exclusions: every write to the counter is gated by the market's authority proven via a SIGNATURE — a Signer<> on that authority, a PDA-signed CPI WHERE the signing PDA is derived from seeds sourced from the market account's own on-chain state (its key or a field loaded from it — NOT a caller-supplied market id from instruction data) that bind it to THIS specific market, or has_one/constraint WHERE the bound authority account is itself declared Signer<>; a has_one (or key-equality) on a NON-signing account only checks the key (not consent), and a global/unscoped authority PDA that can sign for ANY market, are NOT sufficient
the counter is strictly per-market (not a shared aggregate) and has no cross-market read path

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-005: AccountInfo.realloc() called. Verify (1) account owner == program_id, (2) new size is bounded, (3) rent-exemption maintained after resize. Latent pattern documented in our bounty 5 disclosure (percolator-cli#78 F12) — reachable when the per-program asset cap is lifted. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-005.
exclusions: account.owner == program_id is checked before the realloc
the new size is bounded by a validated cap AND rent-exemption is re-funded after the resize

the account is newly allocated in THIS instruction AND its size is verified == 0 before the realloc (size==0 is mandatory, not optional; additionally any lamports were transferred by the program, not pre-funded by an attacker), so no attacker-supplied prior state or size can exist

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-006: raw `AccountInfo` (no Signer<>/Account<> type). If this account is a privileged CALLER, verify `account.is_signer == true` before mutating state, or use Anchor's `Signer<>`. (A documented `/// CHECK:` account used only as a CPI target / program ID / read-only ref is fine — this is a heuristic flag.) See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-006.
exclusions: the AccountInfo is a documented `/// CHECK:` used only as a CPI target, program id, or read-only/sysvar ref — not a privileged caller whose signature matters
account.is_signer is asserted (or the field is a Signer<>/Account<>) before any state mutation
the account is never used to authorize a state change or fund movement — on-chain OR by an off-chain consumer of its emitted/logged key

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-007: raw `&*account.data.borrow()` access. Verify `account.owner == program_id` BEFORE deserializing — attacker can pass a same-length account from a different program whose layout matches. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-007.
exclusions: account.owner == program_id (or the expected program) is checked before deserializing
the account is an Anchor `Account<'info, T>` (Anchor enforces the owner) rather than a raw AccountInfo
the bytes are read only for display/logging and are never persisted, emitted in an event, or trusted for any authorization or fund decision — on-chain OR by an off-chain consumer of the emitted data

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-009: `invoke_signed` CPI. Verify the CALLER has authority for this operation BEFORE the CPI — `invoke_signed` just signs with a PDA, it doesn't validate upstream authority. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-009.
exclusions: the caller's authority for THIS SPECIFIC privileged operation is verified (Signer + has_one/constraint binding the caller to the target resource) BEFORE the invoke_signed — a 'trusted target program' or any unrelated upstream Signer check is NOT sufficient

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-010: init_if_needed enables reinit attacks. If the account holds value or grants authority, a second call can drop balances. Use plain `init` with explicit existence checks unless reinit is truly required. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-010.
exclusions: the account holds no lamports, token balances, authority keys, OR access-gating state that a second initialization could reset — access-gating state includes (non-exhaustively) a timestamp / nonce / status used as a lock, AND any field that controls subsequent PDA derivation, account creation, or role assignment
an explicit already-initialized guard rejects a second initialization

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-011: `#[account(close = ...)]`. Verify (1) account is fully drained before close, (2) lamports go to a controlled destination, (3) any token accounts are closed via Token program, not just zeroed. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-011.
exclusions: the account is fully drained (lamports AND any token balances) before close and its data is zeroed, AND it holds no delegated authority over other on-chain resources (mints, PDAs, vaults) that must be explicitly revoked before close
the close destination is program-controlled or a signer-validated key, not an attacker-supplied account

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-013: hardcoded SPL Token program ID. Use `anchor_spl::token::ID` (or `anchor_spl::token_2022::ID` for Token-2022 accounts) so the typed account ensures the right program is invoked. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-013.
exclusions: the typed anchor_spl::token::ID / token_2022::ID is used via a typed Program<> account, not a raw literal

the literal lives only in a test/const and is NEVER reached on any runtime branch for a program id used in a CPI — including behind a #[cfg(feature = ...)] / #[cfg(not(test))] block that ships in ANY production build (verify the call site AND the build's enabled features, not just the declaration; only #[cfg(test)] truly excludes it)

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-014: integer +/-/* without checked_*. Release builds wrap silently — overflow OR subtraction underflow (the classic lamport drain) — and the wrap is the financial bug. Use `a.checked_add(b)` / `checked_sub(b).ok_or(ErrorCode::Overflow)?`. Heuristic flag — already-checked code can ignore. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-014.
exclusions: the operation already uses checked_/try_/saturating_ math with explicit error handling for the financial case
both operands are compile-time-bounded constants that cannot overflow/underflow

the value is non-financial AND does not feed any downstream financial calculation (proven by tracing every use-site, not a 'this field looks non-financial' claim), AND the operands are bounded so the maximum possible result cannot exceed the type's max (proven by an explicit checked bound or a type-level guarantee, not an unverified 'validated range')

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-016: a stored `.bump` is read. Risk: a non-canonical bump — reused via an Anchor `bump = <account>.bump` constraint, or read and fed to `create_program_address` (both accept non-canonical bumps → PDA substitution). SAFE only if the SAME account's bump was set at init via Anchor's bare `bump`/`ctx.bumps` (canonical), NOT a caller-supplied `#[instruction(bump)]` value — verify that init, then dismiss; otherwise it's the bug. For non-constraint reads compare to `find_program_address(seeds, &program_id).1`. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-016.
exclusions: the read is `bump = <account>.bump` (or a bare `seeds = [...], bump` with NO `= target` after bump) on a typed `Account<'info, T>`, AND the SAME account's stored bump was written at init by Anchor's bare `bump` / `ctx.bumps.<name>` (canonical) — NOT a caller-supplied `#[instruction(bump)]` value and NOT a value from create_program_address: verify that exact init site, then dismiss (idiomatic canonical reuse, not a finding). If the init bump is caller-supplied or otherwise non-canonical, this reuse IS the bug — keep it (Anchor's `bump = <expr>` re-derives via create_program_address with the GIVEN bump, so a non-canonical stored bump still validates).
a non-constraint read is validated against the canonical bump before use (e.g. require!(stored == Pubkey::find_program_address(seeds, program_id).1))

the PDA (and its bump) is created in the same instruction using the canonical bump from find_program_address (NOT a caller-supplied bump passed to create_program_address, which accepts any valid off-curve bump and re-introduces the non-canonical-bump bug)

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-017: `unsafe transmute` on account data. Use bytemuck/anchor typed deserialize with explicit length + discriminator checks. transmute skips both. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-017.
exclusions: a typed deserialize with length + discriminator validation precedes any field use
the cast is over a freshly-created, program-owned, length-checked buffer with a verified layout

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-018: hardcoded System Program ID literal (32 ones in quotes — the canonical empty pubkey). Use `solana_program::system_program::ID` so the comparison is type-safe and a future renaming/typo doesn't silently break verification. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-018.
exclusions: the program-id comparison uses the imported system_program::ID type-safely, not a raw string literal

the literal appears only in a #[cfg(test)] module or a const that is never reached on a runtime program-id verification — a #[cfg(feature = ...)] block that ships in a production build does NOT qualify

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-019: `try_deserialize_unchecked` skips the 8-byte discriminator check. An attacker can pass a different account type with matching length. Use `try_deserialize` (with discriminator check) unless you've already verified the discriminator manually. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-019.
exclusions: try_deserialize (with the discriminator check) is used, or the 8-byte discriminator is verified manually before the unchecked deserialize
the SAME account being deserialized is declared as an Anchor `Account<'info, T>` field (which enforces the discriminator) — not merely that some other account in the same handler is Anchor-typed

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-020: SetAuthority CPI. Verify the CURRENT authority matches the expected key BEFORE invoking — without this check, an attacker can hijack ownership of any token account that flows through this handler. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-020.
exclusions: the current authority is verified to equal the expected key before the SetAuthority CPI

an Anchor `constraint = <signer>.key() == <resource>.authority` on a Signer<> (or has_one WHERE the bound authority field is itself declared Signer<>) binds the SIGNING caller to the CURRENT authority of the resource being changed — a bare Signer<> not bound to the stored authority key, OR a has_one/constraint on a NON-signing authority account (key matches but the holder never consents), is NOT sufficient

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-024: `get_price_unchecked` reads a Pyth price with NO staleness or confidence check. Use `get_price_no_older_than(...)` and reject prices whose confidence interval is too wide — a stale or wide-confidence price lets an attacker trade/liquidate at a mispriced value. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-024.
exclusions: get_price_no_older_than (staleness, with a max-age bound that reflects the protocol's real staleness tolerance — u64::MAX or an unreasonably large age is NOT sufficient) AND a confidence-interval bound are both enforced before use

the price feeds a non-economic / display-only path that cannot trigger a trade, liquidation, or any other economic action — neither on-chain NOR via an off-chain consumer (e.g. a keeper reading emitted price events to trigger liquidations, rebalancing, or collateral updates)

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-025: a sysvar (Clock/Rent) read by RAW-deserializing account data instead of `Clock::get()` or `Sysvar::from_account_info` (both of which key-check the account internally). The raw path trusts whatever account is passed, so an attacker supplies a look-alike carrying chosen time/rent values. Fix: use `Clock::get()` / Anchor `Sysvar<>`; never hand-deserialize a sysvar account. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-025.
exclusions: Clock::get() / Rent::get() or an Anchor Sysvar<> is used (the account key is checked internally)
the sysvar account key is explicitly verified against the canonical sysvar id before the raw deserialize

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-033: an account field is read after a CPI in the same handler — the CPI can mutate that account (balance/authority/data), and Anchor serves the deserialized copy from BEFORE the call. Call `x.reload()` (or re-read from the AccountInfo) between the CPI and the read. Heuristic flag — fires on CPI-then-field-read proximity; cite exclusion #1 if the account is reload()ed, #2 if the callee provably can't touch it. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-033.
exclusions: the account is reload()ed (or re-deserialized from its AccountInfo) between the CPI and the read

the callee provably cannot mutate the read account — it is not in the CPI's account set and the callee cannot reach it via nested CPI (name the callee and its full account set; 'the callee looks unrelated' is NOT sufficient)
the read value feeds only logs/events, never a gate, an amount computation, or stored state

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-034: direct lamport mutation (`try_borrow_mut_lamports` / `lamports.borrow_mut()`). The runtime conserves the per-instruction lamport SUM, but your internal ledger does not move with it — verify every manual debit/credit updates the matching recorded balance (vault totals, user claims), the debited account stays rent-exempt, and the destination is validated. For system-owned accounts use a transfer CPI instead. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-034.
exclusions: the mutation updates BOTH the lamports and the matching internal balance/claim field in the same instruction (cite both writes), and the debited account remains rent-exempt afterwards

the mutation is the documented rent-refund path of an account close: the destination is validated against stored state (not caller-chosen), and the account's data is zeroed or discarded in the same instruction

the accounts are system-owned and the movement uses a system-program transfer CPI — a manual write on a system-owned account cannot deduct anyway (the runtime rejects it); flag it as dead/misleading code

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-029: transaction sent with preflight simulation disabled (`skipPreflight: true`). A blind send eats reverts and fees and can desync a live bot/keeper. Either drop `skipPreflight`, or call `simulateTransaction()` and assert `err === null` (inspecting logs/compute units) BEFORE sending to mainnet. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-029.
exclusions: preflight stays on, or simulateTransaction is called and err === null is asserted before the mainnet send

skipPreflight: true is on a devnet/test/throwaway path, not a value-moving mainnet send — AND the gate selecting it FAILS CLOSED (defaults to preflight ON for mainnet): an env check like `CLUSTER !== 'mainnet-beta'` that yields skipPreflight when the var is unset does NOT qualify; require an explicit non-mainnet allowlist

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-030: hardcoded priority fee (`microLamports: <constant>`). A static compute-unit price underpays during congestion (the tx never lands) or overpays when the network is idle. Derive it from `getRecentPrioritizationFees()` (or a fee oracle) and clamp to a sane max. (`microLamports: 0` — the intentional no-priority-fee opt-out — does not fire.) See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-030.
exclusions: the priority fee is derived from getRecentPrioritizationFees() / a fee oracle and clamped to a sane max
microLamports: 0 (the intentional no-priority opt-out) or a documented test/config default

patterns.reminder: Jelleo SOL-031: Jupiter quote consumed without a `contextSlot` freshness check. Quotes go stale within a few slots; executing an old route means a worse fill and MEV/sandwich exposure. Capture `quoteResponse.contextSlot` and refetch (or reject) if it lags the current slot before you swap. Heuristic flag — fires on Jupiter quote usage (any `api.jup.ag` host or the `@jup-ag/api` client); ignore if you already gate on `contextSlot`. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-031.
exclusions: quoteResponse.contextSlot is captured and the route is refetched/rejected when it lags the current slot
the quote is consumed within the same slot as the fetch (an undefined 'freshness window' is not sufficient — prefer ex1's explicit contextSlot check) AND a slippage bound protects the fill
